verses.1: By the rivers of Babylon we sat mourning and weeping when we remembered Zion.
verses.2: On the poplars of that land we hung up our harps.
verses.3: There our captors asked us for the words of a song; Our tormentors, for a joyful song: "Sing for us a song of Zion!"
verses.4: But how could we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
verses.5: If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand wither.
verses.6: May my tongue stick to my palate if I do not remember you, If I do not exalt Jerusalem beyond all my delights.
verses.7: Remember, LORD, against Edom that day at Jerusalem. They said: "Level it, level it down to its foundations!"
verses.8: Fair Babylon, you destroyer, happy those who pay you back the evil you have done us!
verses.9: Happy those who seize your children and smash them against a rock.

notes.text: Poplars: sometimes incorrectly translated "willow." The Euphrates poplar is a high tree common on riverbanks in the Orient.
Happy those who seize your children and smash them against a rock: the infants represent the future generations, and so must be destroyed if the enemy is truly to be eradicated.
